transcript.text: My indesit washing machine fills with water and drains but the drum just doesn't go round at all. Its an IWC something. Had it about 9 years. Is it worth fixing?

At nine years old, an Indesit washing machine that fills and drains but won't spin is a very common scenario. The most likely cause is simply that the drive belt has snapped or slipped off its pulleys due to age and wear; this is a relatively inexpensive part to replace. Another possibility, given the age, is that the motor's carbon brushes have worn down completely, which stops the motor from turning even if it tries to start. To distinguish between these, I need you to check behind the small square access panel on the bottom right of the front casing (after tilting the machine back safely). Please let me know if the belt is visible and intact, or if it's missing/broken.

I can't see any small square access panel on the front of mine, just the door, the soap drawer and the control panel. The machine is freestanding in a utility room and can be pulled out, so I could get at the back if needed. I did notice a faint hot electrical smell a few weeks ago, but not since. Where exactly should I be looking?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Since your model doesn't have the front access panel, we need to check the rear. On many Indesit machines of this age, the drive belt is located behind a small square metal plate on the bottom right corner of the back casing. Please tilt the machine back safely (get help if needed) and look for this plate. If you find it, unscrew it and check if the rubber belt is still intact around the large drum pulley.

I've unplugged it and pulled it out. There's no small square plate on the back that I can see, so I took the whole back panel off instead. The belt is on the pulleys and feels tight, so it doesn't look broken or slipped. What should I check next, given the smell I mentioned?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
The most likely cause is that the carbon brushes inside your drive motor have worn down. These are small graphite blocks that press against the spinning part of the motor; when they wear out, the motor can't turn even though it might hum or try to start. To check this safely with the machine unplugged, look at the ends of the motor (where the belt connects) and see if you can spot these two black blocks. If they are very short (less than 1cm long) or broken, that suggests the fault. If they look fine, the issue is likely a failed motor or its control module, which would require an engineer to replace.

I can see two blocks on the motor and took them out. One is very short and blackened or charred at the tip, and the other is a bit longer. Does that point to the brushes, and is it safe to replace them myself given the burnt look?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Yes, that points directly to worn carbon brushes. The short, charred brush means it has lost contact with the motor's commutator, which explains why the drum won't turn and also caused the hot electrical smell from sparking inside the motor. To order the correct parts, I need your model number; please look for the rating plate on the inside of the door rim or on the back of the machine.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
I looked at the label inside the door and it says IWC 71252. I can't read any more than that, I'm afraid. Is that enough to find the right brushes, and is it safe to fit them given the burnt tip?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Yes, 'IWC 71252' is enough to find the correct replacement brushes. Regarding safety: it is safe for you to fit them yourself provided the machine remains unplugged and cool. However, because there was a burning smell and one brush was charred, please inspect the motor housing for any melted plastic or scorch marks before fitting the new ones. If the casing looks undamaged, you can proceed with the replacement. Once fitted, plug the machine back in and try a spin programme to confirm it works.
